To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we develop a new shrinkage estimator of large-dimensional covariance matrix by combining a sample estimator and a structured target, where the shrinkage intensity is analytically obtained under normality and estimated by plug-in technique under nonnormality, and that the new estimator performs as well as or even better than the competitors in terms of estimation error and classification error.

we propose two classes of available intensity functions for the shrinkage estimation of covariance matrix in both normal and non-normal settings, which have comparable performance to that of the optimal oracle intensity in the simulation studies.

1) the proposed optimal intensities can achieve the optimal performance in terms of estimation error and prediction error for large-dimensional data, 2) the proposed optimal intensity for nonnormal distribution can be applied to any structured target matrix, and 3) the proposed optimal estimator for nonnormal distribution is more robust than the estimator for normal distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of covariance matrix of large-dimensional data.
the estimation of large covariance matrix by shrinkage.
the estimation of large covariance matrices by shrinking to structured target under both normality and non-normality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed shrinkage covariance estimators perform very favorably in comparison with the competitors.
the proposed shrinkage estimator is a very good alternative to the sample covariance matrix for large-dimensional data in both normal and non-normal distributions.
the proposed method is very effective for large dimensional covariance matrix estimation, which is of interest to many statistical applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal shrinkage intensity is derived analytically for the general target matrix and the optimal shrinkage estimator is obtained for any target matrix under the normality and non-normality.
the optimal oracle intensity is obtained analy-tically for any prespecific target, and two classes of available intensities are proposed for normal and nonnormal data, respectively.
the proposed estimators can be applied for large-dimensional data in both normal and non-normal settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optimal shrinkage estimators can be constructed by convexly mixing the sample covariance matrix with any prespecified structured target in a class which includes various structured covariance estimators.
the proposed shrinkage estimator can be used as an alternative to the sample covariance matrix in large-dimensional data analysis.
the proposed shrinkage estimators can provide an efficient and reliable estimation of large-dimensional covariances for both normal and non-normal distributions.
